messages.author: c280ed21b9da641e
messages.subject: Support for data.tables?
parts:
I have started using data.tables (the data.table package) quite a bit. You can think of it as data.frames on steroids.

What would it take for me to be able to view data.tables within the Deducer viewer, etc.? Currently data.tables are extending data.frames and are easily convertible to data.frames (with as.data.frame()).

The structure of a data.table is as follows:

structure(list(a = structure(1:3, .Label = c("a", "b", "c"), class = "factor"),
b = 1:3), .Names = c("a", "b"), class = c("data.table", "data.frame"
), row.names = c(NA, -3L), sorted = "a")

As you can see, the class indeed does extend "data.frame", but my data.table variables do not appear in the Deducer viewer.

Although, I could convert my data.tables to simple data.frames to use Deducer, I have to convert it back before I can continue -- which is (unnecessarily) tedious.

Is there a way Deducer could work with data.tables?


Thanks,
Harish

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Support for data.tables?
parts:
Harish,

JGR now supports objects inheriting data.frame. This will be included in the next version of JGR. For now, you can use the dev version with:

install.packages('JGR',,'http://www.rforge.net/')


best,
Ian

messages.author: 730176d3d8b81629
messages.subject: Re: Support for data.tables?
parts:
Did JGR or Deducer revert to their behavior before Ian's 2010 note, so that data.table's are no longer visible in the Deducer Data Viewer, or is there something I can do to make them visible?  With the syntax below both of the data frames, but neither of the data tables, will appear in Data Viewer's drop-down list.  This is using R 2.15.2 with JGR GUI 1.7-11, Deducer 0.7.5, and data.table 1.8.6 in Windows XP.  I updated all of my packages to their latest CRAN versions.  Some of the "identical" tests were taken from Matthew Doyle's example(data.table) output.  Thanks!

Mike

set.seed(3); dframe1 <- data.frame(a=runif(5), b=rnorm(5))
set.seed(3); dframe2 <- data.frame(a=runif(5), b=rnorm(5))  ## both appear in Data Viewer dropdown
set.seed(3); dtable1 <- data.table(a=runif(5), b=rnorm(5))
set.seed(3); dtable2 <- data.table(a=runif(5), b=rnorm(5))

identical(dframe1, dframe2) ## TRUE
identical(dframe1, dtable1) ## FALSE
identical(dframe1$a, dtable1$a) ## TRUE
is.data.frame(dtable1) ## TRUE
is.data.frame(dframe1) ## TRUE
is.list(dframe1) ## TRUE
is.list(dtable1) ## TRUE

best,

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Support for data.tables?
parts:
Hi Mike,

Indeed support for data.tables in the default data viewer was
deprecated. There have been a lot of changes to the data viewer since
2010. It is now extensible, and supports very big data.frames.

If you would like to add support for data.tables, you can extend the
viewer. See DeducerSpatial and DeducerText for examples of how this is
done.


Best,
Ian
